LAW AND MOTION 301, ARGUED AND THE COURT RULED AS FOLLOWS: PETITIONERS R HINES, AND JANE HINES' NOTICE OF HEARING ON MERITS IS DENIED. THERE IS SUBSTANTIAL EVIDENCE TO SHOW THAT RESPONDENTS' CONCLUSION THAT THE PROJECT DOES NOT VIOLATE THE LOCAL COASTAL PLAN IS THERE AND THAT IS SUFFICIENT TO UPHOLD THOSE DETERMINATIONS. PETITIONER HAS NOT SHOWN THAT AN EXCEPTION TO THE CEQA CATEGORICAL EXEMPTION NO MATTER WHAT STANDARD APPLIES. THERE IS AMPLE EVIDENCE SUGGESTING THAT THERE IS NOT ANY IMPACT ON THE ENVIRONMENT AND NO SIGNIFICANT EVIDENCE WHICH GOES THE OTHER WAY. EVEN IF A FAIR ARGUMENT STANDARD APPLIED, IT IS NOT MET HERE AND CERTAINLY WOULD NOT BE MET UNDER A SIGNIFICANT EVIDENCE STANDARD. MR. PERRY TO SUBMIT A PROPOSED FORM OF ORDER. PETITIONER'S EXCERPTS OF RECORDS AND RESPONDENTS' BOARD OF SUPERVISORS AND REAL PARTIES IN INTERESTS' CONDENSED RECORD IN SUPPORT OF OPPOSITION TO TRIAL BRIEF, BOTH LODGED WITH THE COURT, WERE RETURNED TO THEIR RESPECTIVE PARTIES. PER DIEM FEES WERE ASSESSED. (301/PJB) JUDGE: PETER J. BUSCH, REPORTER: CAROL KAREN, CSR# 8189

LAW AND MOTION 301, THE COURT VACATED IT TENTATIVE RULING AND DENIED PETITIONER R HINES, JANE HINES' NOTICE OF MOTION TO TAX COSTS. THE TENTATIVE RULING WAS BASED ON MISSAPPREHENSION THAT THE PETITIONER UOPON RECEIPT OF THE ESTIMATE FROM THE COMMISSION ABOUT THE COST TO PREPARE THE RECORD HAD THE OPTION TO PREPARE THE RECORD THEMSELVES AS A RESULT, THE COURT WAS DISABASED OF THAT AND THEREFORE CHANGED THE TENTATIVE RULING AND DENIED THE MOTION TO TAX COSTS. RESPONDENT TO SUBMIT FORM OF ORDER. JUDGE: HAROLD E.
